references.text: The murder of Abel – the first righteous one to be killed. Cain struck down his brother Abel, and his blood cried out from the ground. Jesus refers to this as the beginning of the series of righteous blood that was shed ([ref:Gen 4:8|Genesis 4:8]).

The murder of Zechariah, son of the priest Jehoiada, who was stoned in the courtyard of the Lord's house. This is the Zechariah Jesus refers to – the one killed between the altar and the temple building. As he died, Zechariah said: "May the Lord see this and call you to account!" ([ref:2 Chron 24:20-22|2 Chronicles 24:20-22]).

Abel's blood cries out from the ground to God, showing that the blood of the righteous demands justice from God – a theme Jesus addresses when he says all this blood will be required of this generation ([ref:Gen 4:10|Genesis 4:10]).

The Letter to the Hebrews mentions that by faith Abel offered a better sacrifice than Cain, and that through his faith he still speaks even after his death. Abel is the first righteous martyr Jesus refers to ([ref:Heb 11:4|Hebrews 11:4]).

Jesus' blood speaks more powerfully than Abel's blood. Abel's blood cried out for vengeance, but Jesus' blood speaks of reconciliation – a contrast that deepens the theme of the blood of the righteous ([ref:Heb 12:24|Hebrews 12:24]).

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus mentions the same series of righteous martyrs from Abel to Zechariah, son of Berekja, and says all this will come upon this generation ([ref:Matt 23:35-36|Matthew 23:35-36]).

The slain martyrs cry out from under the altar, asking how long it will be before the Lord judges and avenges their blood – an eschatological parallel to the idea that the blood of the righteous must be required ([ref:Rev 6:10|Revelation 6:10]).

In Babylon was found the blood of prophets and saints, and of all who have been slaughtered on earth. This reflects Jesus' words that all prophetic blood will be required of this generation ([ref:Rev 18:24|Revelation 18:24]).
